selector.rationale: Decisive findings of lumbar spinal tenderness, bilateral leg weakness, and MRI signal changes at L4–L5 best explained by Spondylodiscitis, with Enterobacter cloacae infection being a likely cause.

rejected.label: Enterobacter cloacae infection
rejected.why: While Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound and blood, it is more likely the cause of the Spondylodiscitis rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Anastomotic fistula
rejected.why: Although the patient had a refractory anastomotic fistula, the current symptoms and findings are more consistent with a spinal infection.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis is a possible diagnosis, but Spondylodiscitis better explains the specific findings of spinal tenderness and signal changes at L4–L5.

rejected.label: Epidural abscess
rejected.why: While an epidural abscess is possible, the lack of sensory loss and the specific MRI findings make Spondylodiscitis a more likely diagnosis.
